trust_zones.name: Public request edge
trust_zones.description: Untrusted browsers, API clients and external MCP clients reach a single public domain.

trust_zones.name: User-controlled browser context
trust_zones.description: Cookies, redirects, local state and client-side rendering are controlled by an untrusted user agent.

trust_zones.name: AMOS application policy
trust_zones.description: Trusted request parsing, authentication, current authorization, routing and application decisions.

trust_zones.name: PostgreSQL data plane
trust_zones.description: Tenant records, identity state, grants, billing events and migration ledger.

trust_zones.name: Workspace data compartment
trust_zones.description: A selected personal workspace or organization is an isolated resource/billing scope, not an identity or ambient authority.

trust_zones.name: External provider callbacks
trust_zones.description: Identity, payment, email and cloud-provider requests and credentials cross an external boundary.

trust_zones.name: Separate business service
trust_zones.description: Private business-service origin reached only through the authenticated AMOS proxy boundary.

trust_zones.name: Owner operational controls
trust_zones.description: Owner-controlled credentials, maintenance policy, pause controls and private application operations.

trust_zones.name: Untrusted coding workspace
trust_zones.description: Isolated code agents consume hostile repository text and produce candidate changes without production authority.

trust_zones.name: Independent verification
trust_zones.description: Separate verifier identity and workspace check candidate source and denied paths.

trust_zones.name: Trusted build
trust_zones.description: A qualified builder creates artifacts from an exact reviewed source and toolchain.

trust_zones.name: Release authority
trust_zones.description: Independent release identity evaluates current policy, pause state and artifact attestations.

trust_zones.name: Owner installation
trust_zones.description: An owner-controlled AMOS deployment accepts only authorized current releases.

trust_zones.name: Owner application repository
trust_zones.description: Private business code, custom UI, infrastructure and managed-file ownership baselines.

trust_zones.name: Untrusted diagnostic and repository input
trust_zones.description: Logs, crash output, README text, PRs, tool output and external evidence are data, never authority or instructions.

trust_zones.name: Sanitized upstream reporting
trust_zones.description: An optional public upstream destination receives only typed allowlisted diagnostics.

trust_zones.name: AMSL maintainer boundary
trust_zones.description: Independent shared-library maintainers retain their own review and release authority.

trust_zones.name: External customer agent runtime
trust_zones.description: Independent agent runtime connects through standard MCP; broad agent governance remains outside AMOS.

principals.name: Anonymous caller
principals.authority: May send bounded unauthenticated requests only.
principals.explicitly_not: Cannot select a tenant, create a principal or invoke protected operations.

principals.name: User-controlled browser context
principals.authority: Sends UI requests and holds only the application-issued browser session artifact.
principals.explicitly_not: DOM state, local data, referrer, redirect target or CSRF request cannot assert identity or authority.

principals.name: Authenticated person in a browser
principals.authority: Presents credentials and requests a selected personal or organization workspace.
principals.explicitly_not: A valid session alone does not prove current membership, resource ownership, entitlement or step-up assurance.

principals.name: Customer API-key client
principals.authority: Presents a machine credential bound to an explicit owner, tenant, resource and scope.
principals.explicitly_not: Cannot expand its stored scope or impersonate a person.

principals.name: External MCP client
principals.authority: Calls eligible operations through the declared OAuth/client profile.
principals.explicitly_not: Protocol access does not bypass AMOS authorization or customer-runtime governance.

principals.name: Identity provider
principals.authority: Returns an external authentication response for a registered client.
principals.explicitly_not: Email or callback parameters alone do not establish AMOS identity or workspace authority.

principals.name: Payment provider
principals.authority: Signs provider events and exposes an authoritative account snapshot.
principals.explicitly_not: Event order or a signed stale event alone cannot reverse current payment policy.

principals.name: Separate business service
principals.authority: Handles only explicitly allowlisted requests with authenticated propagated identity.
principals.explicitly_not: Cannot trust client-supplied identity headers or become a public bypass around AMOS.

principals.name: Application owner/operator
principals.authority: Controls local maintenance policy, credentials, retention and pause/recovery actions.
principals.explicitly_not: Owner app credentials do not grant unrelated upstream or AMSL maintainer authority.

principals.name: Maintenance coding agent
principals.authority: Produces a candidate patch in an isolated workspace under scoped job limits.
principals.explicitly_not: Has no production, verifier, builder, releaser, policy-edit or unrestricted egress authority.

principals.name: Independent verifier
principals.authority: Runs required checks against exact candidate source and reports evidence.
principals.explicitly_not: Cannot author or approve the candidate, alter mandatory checks, sign a release or obtain production credentials.

principals.name: Trusted builder
principals.authority: Builds an artifact from an approved immutable source and declared toolchain.
principals.explicitly_not: Cannot choose policy, approve source, promote an artifact or deploy to an owner installation.

principals.name: Independent release identity
principals.authority: Evaluates verified source/artifact identity against current owner policy and target generation.
principals.explicitly_not: Cannot waive missing verification, stale generation, revoked identity or pause state.

principals.name: External repository contributor
principals.authority: Submits untrusted source and metadata for isolated validation.
principals.explicitly_not: Cannot read privileged secrets, mutate trusted caches or supply the trusted release artifact.

principals.name: Author of hostile log or repository text
principals.authority: May control text ingested by a diagnostic or maintenance job.
principals.explicitly_not: Text cannot change job scope, policy, authority, required checks or permitted egress.

principals.name: AMSL maintainer
principals.authority: Reviews and releases shared AMSL code under AMSL governance.
principals.explicitly_not: AMOS automation cannot grant or assume AMSL merge/release authority.

principals.name: AMOS upstream reporting service
principals.explicitly_not: Cannot receive raw logs, business data, secrets or identifying infrastructure details.

critical_assets.name: Credentials, sessions and proof challenges
critical_assets.impact: Credential disclosure or stale acceptance can grant an unauthorized identity.

critical_assets.name: Customer API keys and MCP OAuth grants
critical_assets.impact: A verifier or grant-binding failure can widen machine authority across resources or tenants.

critical_assets.name: Principal, workspace, membership, grant and assurance state
critical_assets.impact: Stale, confused or cross-tenant authority exposes protected operations or resources.

critical_assets.name: Personal and organization business data
critical_assets.impact: A tenant-boundary failure exposes or modifies another workspace's data.

critical_assets.name: Payment, subscription and usage state
critical_assets.impact: Replay or stale projection can grant paid access, charge incorrectly or lose a financial event.

critical_assets.name: Provider credentials and signing secrets
critical_assets.impact: Credential exposure enables provider impersonation or unauthorized effects.

critical_assets.name: Private owner source, custom UI and infrastructure
critical_assets.impact: Exfiltration or overwrite can disclose private code or destroy owner-authored behavior.

critical_assets.name: Logs, crashes, traces and diagnostic payloads
critical_assets.impact: Unbounded or raw export can disclose secrets, business data or infrastructure identity.

critical_assets.name: Source, build inputs, attestations and release artifacts
critical_assets.impact: Substitution or wrong identity can authorize unreviewed code for an owner installation.

critical_assets.name: Installed generation, policy revision and pause state
critical_assets.impact: A stale approval or missed pause can roll back newer code or override owner policy.

critical_assets.name: Database schema and migration ledger
critical_assets.impact: Changed or misordered migrations can corrupt data or weaken authorization invariants.

critical_assets.name: Request, parser, worker and provider capacity
critical_assets.impact: Unbounded work or hostile input can exhaust service or durable resources.

controls.requirement: Resolve one immutable principal after proof; select only a personally owned or currently joined workspace; recheck live membership, grant, entitlement and resource tenant at each boundary, failing closed on unknown freshness.

denied_path_test.name: TestCrossTenantAndStaleMembershipDenied
denied_path_test.assertion: A valid credential with mismatched tenant, revoked membership, expired grant or unprovable freshness is denied without exposing resource existence.

controls.residual_risk: No application authorization implementation or composed tenant-isolation evidence exists yet.

controls.requirement: Expire and revoke opaque sessions on account disablement, credential recovery and owner lifecycle changes; read current session state before protected handler access.

denied_path_test.name: TestExpiredRevokedOrDisabledSessionDenied
denied_path_test.assertion: An expired, revoked or disabled session cannot reach a protected handler; unavailable authoritative session state does not allow access.

controls.residual_risk: Session storage, lifecycle consistency bounds and provider-specific recovery behavior remain unqualified.

controls.requirement: Bind a resumable proof challenge to the verified actor, workspace, operation digest, required assurance and expiry; consume it once and re-evaluate current authority after proof.

denied_path_test.name: TestProofCannotResumeDifferentActorTenantOrOperation
denied_path_test.assertion: Changing actor, tenant, operation or assurance after proof, or replaying/expiring the challenge, is denied without a bypass.

controls.residual_risk: Proof assurance levels, challenge persistence and provider-specific factors require qualification.

controls.requirement: Treat API keys and MCP OAuth grants as narrow credentials only; bind resource and tenant, apply current membership/policy on every invocation, and route eligible MCP operations through the same handler and decision as web and REST.

denied_path_test.name: TestAPIKeyAndMCPGrantCannotCrossTenant
denied_path_test.assertion: A key or MCP grant scoped to one resource/workspace cannot discover or invoke another tenant's operation.

controls.residual_risk: The supported MCP OAuth/client profile and real client behavior still require qualification; AMOS does not provide broad customer-agent governance.

controls.requirement: Verify provider signatures over bounded raw request bytes before durable receipt; atomically deduplicate event identity and payload digest before acknowledging, and reconcile unknown outcomes.

denied_path_test.name: TestWebhookReplayAndConflictingDigestDenied
denied_path_test.assertion: An invalid signature creates no inbox row; an exact replay has one effect and a conflicting duplicate cannot overwrite accepted event state.

controls.residual_risk: Provider signature key rotation, durable database behavior and real provider event qualification remain open gates.

controls.requirement: Treat provider-authoritative reconciliation as the source of current subscription state; event order, retry or stale worker completion cannot reinstate older access or reverse a newer financial result.

denied_path_test.name: TestOutOfOrderEventCannotRestoreStalePaidState
denied_path_test.assertion: A delayed older provider snapshot/event does not restore paid access or overwrite a newer confirmed state.

controls.residual_risk: Provider reconciliation freshness, outage policy, concurrency and live account evidence are not implemented.

controls.requirement: Bind identity-provider callbacks to one-time state, nonce and PKCE context, validate redirect targets, and reject replay or mismatched issuer/client/workspace context before creating an authenticated session.

denied_path_test.name: TestCallbackFromOtherBrowserOrProviderCannotLoginOrLink
denied_path_test.assertion: A callback from another browser/provider, with absent state or an unapproved redirect, creates no session and links no identity.

controls.residual_risk: Concrete identity provider assurance and callback composition remain unqualified.

controls.requirement: Normalize and bound public requests before mutation; enforce CSRF and host policy, rate/body limits and non-enumerating errors at sensitive identity boundaries.

denied_path_test.name: TestForgedHostCSRFAndOversizeDeniedWithoutSideEffect
denied_path_test.assertion: A forged Host, invalid CSRF token or oversized body is rejected with the documented status and no durable side effect.

controls.residual_risk: Limits, cookie attributes and proxy deployment settings require implementation and live profile checks.

controls.requirement: Route separate-service calls only to a private configured origin and exact allowlist; strip caller credentials and identity headers, authenticate propagated identity, validate forwarded host/redirects, and enforce timeout/body/streaming bounds.

denied_path_test.name: TestProxyRejectsSpoofedIdentityAndUntrustedDestination
denied_path_test.assertion: Client-supplied identity headers, unapproved destination/redirect and invalid forwarded-host values never reach the business service.

controls.residual_risk: The separate-service implementation, authenticated propagation and non-bypass deployment evidence do not exist.

controls.requirement: Reject ambiguous path encodings, dot segments, duplicate separators, unknown operation-policy fields and generator mappings that would lose actor, tenant, entitlement, assurance, side-effect, retry or MCP exposure policy.

denied_path_test.name: TestAlternateEncodingCannotBypassReservedOrPolicyBoundary
denied_path_test.assertion: Equivalent or malformed encodings cannot reach an unreserved route or change the required authorization policy; seed and fuzz tests preserve the deny result.

controls.residual_risk: The router, OpenAPI policy extension and generated API/MCP code are not implemented or fuzz-qualified.

controls.requirement: Construct upstream diagnostics from a new typed allowlist, exclude raw logs/business data/secrets/paths/addresses, bound and validate payloads, and make reporting optional and independent of application service.

denied_path_test.name: TestCanaryAbsentFromEveryForbiddenOutputChannel
denied_path_test.assertion: Synthetic canaries in nested, encoded and raw diagnostic fields never appear in previews, logs, telemetry export or browser artifacts.

controls.residual_risk: No typed diagnostic exporter, retention control or canary evidence exists.

controls.requirement: Treat logs, crashes, repository files and tool output as untrusted data, not job authorization; constrain job scope, credentials and egress, and block secret/private-source exfiltration even when hostile text instructs an agent to do so.

denied_path_test.name: TestHostileInstructionsCannotExfiltrateCanaryOrPrivateSource
denied_path_test.assertion: Injected instructions cannot change job scope or release authority and no canary/private source reaches a disallowed destination in the selected runtime sandbox.

controls.residual_risk: No selected runtime sandbox or real egress-denial qualification exists; mocks alone are insufficient.

controls.requirement: Use distinct, scoped identities and credentials for coder, verifier, builder and releaser; coding cannot access production secrets or modify policy/mandatory checks, and verification runs independently against exact source.

denied_path_test.name: TestCandidateCannotApproveOrForgeItsOwnVerification
denied_path_test.assertion: Candidate-controlled tests, reports or policy edits cannot satisfy required checks or grant verifier, builder, releaser or deployment authority.

controls.residual_risk: Credential stores, isolation, trusted check manifest and distinct principals are proposed, not implemented.

controls.requirement: Run third-party contributions without privileged secrets or writes to trusted caches/artifacts, then rebuild the reviewed source in a trusted environment before release.

denied_path_test.name: TestUntrustedPRCannotReadSecretsOrWriteTrustedArtifact
denied_path_test.assertion: A third-party PR receives no privileged secret and cannot poison a cache or artifact later accepted by the trusted release path.

controls.residual_risk: Workflow trust roots, runner isolation and trusted post-review rebuild remain unqualified.

controls.requirement: Bind release authorization to immutable source, builder identity, artifact digest, current policy revision and installation; revoking a builder/release identity invalidates cached eligibility and identifies affected artifacts.

denied_path_test.name: TestWrongOrRevokedReleaseIdentityBlocksPromotion
denied_path_test.assertion: A valid signature from the wrong, revoked or source-mismatched identity cannot authorize a release.

controls.residual_risk: No trusted builder profile, immutable attestation verifier or release identity has been qualified.

controls.requirement: On dependency or credential compromise, revoke the identity, identify affected artifacts by immutable provenance, hold promotion and require fresh trusted evidence before recovery.

denied_path_test.name: TestRevokedBuilderCannotAuthorizeRecoveryRelease
denied_path_test.assertion: A revoked identity and previously cached attestation cannot clear an incident hold or authorize recovery.

controls.residual_risk: Incident procedures, inventory coverage and provider revocation behavior are not qualified.

controls.requirement: Promotion atomically compares the expected installed release generation and re-evaluates current policy and pause state; stale approval cannot deploy over a newer accepted release.

denied_path_test.name: TestReleaseIdentityAndReplay
denied_path_test.assertion: Release A approved against generation N is rejected after release B advances the target to N+1.

controls.residual_risk: No atomic promotion adapter, current-policy recheck or live installation evidence exists.

controls.requirement: Persist a monotonic owner pause generation and check it at queue claim, provider call, verification and promotion; resume requires reconciliation and current policy, never blind replay.

denied_path_test.name: TestPauseGenerationWinsPromotionRace
denied_path_test.assertion: If pause races with eligibility or promotion, the current pause generation blocks subsequent launch and release; unknown reachability remains explicitly unresolved.

controls.residual_risk: Pause durability, all reachable installation checks and disconnected-agent behavior remain unimplemented.

controls.requirement: Keep revocation and authority epochs outside rollback-prone application data or require a freshness barrier before activation; restored credentials/grants never silently regain authority.

denied_path_test.name: TestRestoreDoesNotResurrectRevokedCredential
denied_path_test.assertion: After restoring an older database snapshot, revoked credentials remain denied until fresh authority is established; unknown freshness holds activation.

controls.residual_risk: Restore authority placement, real database snapshot testing and provider-live recovery remain open gates.

controls.requirement: Use a versioned ownership manifest and three-way comparison; never overwrite owner-customized files based only on a generated-path name, and stop on unresolved conflicts.

denied_path_test.name: TestCustomizedFileIsNeverSilentlyOverwritten
denied_path_test.assertion: A changed owner file is retained and an actionable conflict is reported until an owner-controlled resolution.

controls.residual_risk: Upgrade ownership metadata and conflict handling are not yet implemented.

controls.requirement: Bind migration identity to the SHA-256 of exact source bytes in the applying transaction and hard-stop when an already-applied ID has changed content.

denied_path_test.name: TestChangedAppliedMigrationFailsWithoutDataLoss
denied_path_test.assertion: Changed source for an applied migration ID is rejected and existing data remains intact.

controls.residual_risk: No integrated migration registry or real PostgreSQL migration evidence is present in this worktree.

threats.attack: A valid session selects another person's workspace, stale organization membership, expired grant or resource ID from a different tenant.
threats.expected_decision: Deny unless verified subject, currently active membership/grant, workspace ownership, entitlement and resource tenancy all match current authoritative state; use non-enumerating response where existence is sensitive.

threats.attack: A stolen, expired, disabled or revoked session is replayed after account, credential or membership lifecycle change.
threats.expected_decision: Deny stale/revoked credentials and re-evaluate current account, membership and grant state before protected handler access.

threats.attack: A valid proof challenge is replayed, expired or resumed under a changed actor, workspace or operation to satisfy a different sensitive mutation.
threats.expected_decision: Consume challenge once, require exact actor/workspace/operation/assurance binding and evaluate current authority again after proof.

threats.attack: A machine key, OAuth grant, client-supplied tenant, MCP argument or discovery endpoint is used to widen scope or cross a private tenant boundary.
threats.expected_decision: Deny any operation outside current key/grant binding and current app policy; MCP discovery/invocation uses the same handler, tenant checks, entitlements and assurance as REST/web.

threats.attack: Forged, stale, replayed or conflicting payment events cause duplicate durable effects or grant access before verified receipt.
threats.expected_decision: Verify signature and bounded raw bytes before receipt; deduplicate identical provider event identity and reject conflicting digest before acknowledgement or effect.

threats.attack: Delayed webhook, stale worker or unknown provider outcome reverses newer subscription state, repeats charge intent or grants stale entitlements.
threats.expected_decision: Hold uncertain state and reconcile against current provider authority; stale event order cannot reverse current subscription policy or duplicate an external effect.

threats.attack: A cross-site, replayed or issuer/client-mismatched authentication callback creates a session, links an identity or redirects to an attacker-controlled target.
threats.expected_decision: Reject absent, mismatched, expired or consumed state/nonce/PKCE and unapproved redirect before creating session or linking identity.

threats.attack: Host spoofing, CSRF, oversized bodies, ambiguous encoding or unbounded anonymous requests cause mutation, account enumeration or resource exhaustion.
threats.expected_decision: Reject before side effects with bounded resource use and stable non-enumerating response; fail closed on host, CSRF and request-shape policy.

threats.attack: A hostile site or compromised browser context causes a cookie-authenticated mutation, redirects credentials, or relies on untrusted client state for tenant selection.
threats.expected_decision: Reject invalid CSRF and redirect context before mutation; browser state never creates identity, changes tenant authority or suppresses a fresh server-side decision.

threats.attack: A request exploits proxy destination/redirect handling or forged forwarded-host and identity headers to reach an unintended origin or bypass AMOS policy.
threats.expected_decision: Deny requests outside exact private route/origin allowlist; strip untrusted credentials and identity headers, authenticate propagated identity and bound redirect, host, timeout and body behavior.

threats.attack: Alternate URL encodings, duplicate separators, dot segments or generator/schema drift reach a reserved route or drop required policy metadata in REST/MCP generation.
threats.expected_decision: Reject ambiguous syntax and unsupported policy mapping; generation fails closed rather than producing an operation with implicit authorization or exposure.

threats.attack: An attacker places a canary, business record or secret in controlled log/crash text and an unrestricted exporter serializes it to reporting or browser artifacts.
threats.expected_decision: Exclude by construction unless a typed allowlist explicitly permits the bounded field; reject unknown/nested/raw payloads and keep app operation independent of optional reporting.

threats.attack: Malicious log, README, issue, commit or tool output instructs an agent to expose credentials/private source, change its scope or bypass checks.
threats.expected_decision: Treat content as data only; deny disallowed egress and capability changes, with no secret-bearing or private-source channel from the coding job.

threats.attack: A candidate changes its acceptance controls, deletes/forges tests or supplies its own verification result to acquire builder or release authority.
threats.expected_decision: Deny self-approval; independently verify exact candidate source under protected required checks and keep verifier, builder and releaser credentials separate.

threats.attack: Third-party PR executes with privileged credentials, writes a trusted cache, or promotes a PR-built artifact after review.
threats.expected_decision: Deny privileged secret/cache access to untrusted contribution; trusted release must rebuild reviewed source in isolated trusted context and bind exact digest.

threats.attack: A compromised, revoked or wrong builder/release identity signs or replays an artifact to an owner installation; a valid signature is mistaken for approval.
threats.expected_decision: Deny unless immutable source, qualified builder identity, artifact digest, current policy, installation and non-revoked release authority all match; signature alone never approves.

threats.attack: Release A approval is replayed after release B changed installed generation or owner policy, overwriting newer accepted state.
threats.expected_decision: Atomically compare expected installed generation and current policy/pause revision at promotion; reject stale approval and reconcile unknown outcomes.

threats.attack: Eligibility or promotion races with owner pause; stale controller or disconnected agent resumes/replays work after pause.
threats.expected_decision: Pause generation wins at every launch and promotion boundary; report unreachable installations explicitly and require fresh reconciliation/policy when resuming.

threats.attack: An older database backup restores revoked credentials/grants or old maintenance authority and silently reactivates them.
threats.expected_decision: Keep revocation/authority epoch outside rollback-prone state or hold activation until fresh authoritative state is proven; unknown freshness denies authority.

threats.attack: An upgrade classifies a changed custom page, business file or infrastructure file as generated and silently overwrites it.
threats.expected_decision: Preserve owner-authored bytes and stop with an actionable conflict unless an owner-controlled action explicitly resolves the three-way difference.

threats.attack: Migration source bytes change under an already-applied ID or concurrent runners apply an ambiguous schema transition.
threats.expected_decision: Bind exact source SHA-256 to migration ID in the serialized applying transaction; reject changed applied bytes and preserve prior data.
